prompt: how do we know how far away a star is

Earth's orbit gives telescopes a far wider "blink", six months apart, and the star's tiny shift gives away how far off it is. For distant stars, astronomers switch to brightness-based methods. 👍 [CHIPS]What's a light year|Brightness method|Try the thumb trick[/CHIPS]

Sunlight reaching you now left the Sun about eight minutes ago, which makes the Sun eight light-minutes away. The next nearest star is a bit over four light years off. ✨ [CHIPS]Nearest star|Could we travel there|How fast is light[/CHIPS]

A second approach watches the star wobble slightly as an orbiting planet tugs on it. Thousands of exoplanets have been confirmed this way. 🪐 [CHIPS]Transit method|Wobble method|Any like Earth[/CHIPS]
